issues.problem: R11-02 is still incomplete, and part of this round is a regression. Fabricated claims pass the exact SKILL.md gate (verify --strict) with exit 0. (a) The previous round's own end-to-end probes still pass verbatim: the corpus holds trimmed copies of them ('Acme supports SSO' instead of '... for enterprise customers'; 'Acme Cloud is SOC 2 Type II certified' instead of '... for its enterprise platform'), and adding claim words that sit in another quote clause drops the aligned-clause overlap below the 60% threshold in _negation_conflict, so the contradiction is never compared. The corpus is overfitted to the reviewer's literal examples. (b) Regression vs 197a8d6: counting cue parity makes 'Neither Acme nor Initech supports SSO', 'No, Acme does not support SSO' and 'does not support SSO, not even on enterprise plans' read as positive, and splitting quote clauses on 'and' detaches the negation from the second conjunct ('Acme does not support SSO and SCIM' supports 'Acme supports SCIM'; 'never encrypts logs and backups' supports 'encrypts backups'). (c) Classes the documented limits do not cover: typographic apostrophes are not negation (NEGATION_RE has only ASCII n't, so a quote saying 'doesn’t'/'isn’t' supports the positive claim); the currency is parsed but never compared ($50M vs €50M, '50 million dollars' vs '50 million euros'); years are exempt from attachment (ok = True), so swapped or re-attached years pass ('founded in 2015 and acquired in 2019' vs 'founded in 2019 and acquired in 2015'); the head noun only has to be among the quote's first three content words after the figure ('500 enterprise customers' vs '500 staff serving enterprise customers'). quality-gates.md says every figure must match 'the same normalised value and unit' and be 'attached to the same thing', which is not what the code does for currency and years.

issues.suggested_fix: Negation: do not use cue parity across a whole clause (treat 'neither/nor', 'no, not', ', not even' as one negation), do not split on 'and'/'or' inside a negated clause (or distribute the negation over the conjuncts), add U+2019/U+02BC apostrophes to NEGATION_RE (normalise them first), and align a claim clause with any quote clause that contains its entities/figures even when the claim adds words found elsewhere in the quote (lower or drop the 60% token requirement when entities or figures align). Figures: compare the currency symbol/word (dollars/euros/USD/EUR) as part of the unit; give years the same attachment rule as other figures (or document the exemption). Build the corpus from new adversarial pairs, not trimmed copies of reviewer probes, and add the r2 probes verbatim plus the fab5 pairs. If some classes stay out of scope for v1, list each one in quality-gates.md and mark R11-02 partial.

issues.problem: False-positive regression in a9a8968: honest claims that passed the strict gate at 197a8d6 now fail it. The 'head noun' is the first content word after the figure, so any reordering puts a date or qualifier there ('cut prices by 20% in March 2024' -> noun 'march'; '$2.67 billion for fiscal 2024' -> 'fiscal'), and figures without a noun need the two preceding words to precede the quote's figure too ('increased 12% year over year to $5.2 billion' vs 'revenue of $5.2 billion, up 12%'). The new 'and' clause split and cue parity reject honest negations ('works offline without an account' vs 'works offline and without an account'; 'does not support SSO and SCIM' vs 'does not support SSO or SCIM'; 'has no SSO and no audit logs' vs 'offers neither SSO nor audit logs'). Pre-existing but unaddressed by the normalisation: '40 percent' is not '40%', and an ASCII 'doesn't' claim fails against a typographic 'doesn’t' quote. The documented limits mention only paraphrased units ('500 employees' vs '500 people'). FIX-BRIEF: a false positive is a bug and every new block needs honest-variant tests; the honest corpus pairs are all near-verbatim extensions of the claim.

SSO or SCIM' -> HEAD ('partial', 1.0, 'negation mismatch'), 197a8d6 supported; 'Acme has no SSO and no audit logs' vs 'Acme offers neither SSO nor audit logs' -> HEAD partial negation mismatch, 197a8d6 supported. bin/honest4.py: 6/15 realistic paraphrases rejected at HEAD vs 4/15 at 197a8d6. runs/hon5.tsv: '40% ... according to its filing' vs '40 percent ... annual filing' -> partial (number mismatch); ASCII vs curly 'doesn't' -> partial (negation mismatch).
issues.suggested_fix: Attach a figure to its noun phrase rather than the first word after it: skip prepositional/date phrases ('in March 2024', 'for fiscal 2024', 'year over year') or accept a match when the claim's noun appears anywhere in the same quote clause as the figure; for noun-less figures, accept a shared content word anywhere in the clause. Fix negation as in issue 1 (no 'and' split inside negated scope, 'neither/nor' as one negation). Normalise 'percent'/'per cent' to '%' and typographic apostrophes before matching. Add these honest pairs (and reordered/paraphrased ones) to the honest corpus.

issues.problem: Ctrl-C/SIGTERM still lets new worker sessions start. _terminate_live_workers kills the live process group, but inside run_cursor_worker the killed attempt is just an unsuccessful attempt: with SB_CURSOR_MODEL_ALLOW_FALLBACK set, the loop immediately launches the next fallback model; without it, if the killed worker's partial output contains a transient marker ('network', 'reconnecting', 'Connection lost', ...), it sleeps 3 s and relaunches. The dispatcher then waits in ThreadPoolExecutor.__exit__ until that new session ends or times out (600 s by default). SKILL.md says queued workers are cancelled and 'none starts afterwards'.
issues.evidence: REVF-H8a3-probe/bin/sigdrive3.py (dispatcher in its own session, fake cursor fakebin/cursor_rec logging START/TERM, timeout 8 s, concurrency 1): (A) SB_CURSOR_MODEL_ALLOW_FALLBACK=1, SIGTERM at +2.00 s -> '+2.01s TERM pid=2749', '+2.02s START pid=4664 model=claude-opus-4-8-medium-fast AFTER-SIGNAL', TERM only at +10.02 s (its own timeout); dispatcher 'KeyboardInterrupt after 9.9'. (B) default settings, worker printed 'Searching the web: network effects in developer tools', SIGINT at +2.01 s -> '+2.02s TERM', '+5.03s START pid=27233 model=claude-opus-4-8-medium AFTER-SIGNAL', TERM at +13.04 s; dispatcher exits after 12.9 s. The queued-worker case from r2 is fixed (r2 bin/sigdrive.py: no START after the signal, exit at 1.9 s). InterruptTests mock dispatch_agent, so no test covers a running worker's retry/fallback.
issues.suggested_fix: Set a module-level stop Event in the interrupt path (before shutdown/terminate) and check it in _run_cli before Popen (raise KeyboardInterrupt or return a cancelled result) and in run_cursor_worker's fallback/retry loop; add a test with fallback enabled and a transient marker asserting no second launch after the interrupt.

issues.problem: Whether a connection is 'proxied' (connected to as is, no vetting) is decided by comparing urlparse(full_url).hostname with urlparse('//' + req.host).hostname. urllib percent-decodes req.host and keeps the userinfo, so a bibliography URL such as http://169.254.169.254%23@public.example/ makes the two differ with no proxy configured: unsafe_url_reason vets 'public.example', and the connection is then made unpinned to '169.254.169.254#@public.example' through the system resolver. glibc 2.39 refuses to resolve such names, so this is not exploitable on Linux; resolvers that accept '#', '@' or '/' in names (macOS untested) would turn it into a rebinding-style SSRF bypass of the target check.
issues.evidence: REVF-H8a3-probe/bin/differential.py (all proxy env vars removed, resolver returns a public address, socket.create_connection recorded): 'http://169.254.169.254%23@public.example/latest/meta-data/' -> unsafe_url_reason None, req.host '169.254.169.254#@public.example', _is_proxied True, names vetted ['public.example'], create_connection asked for ('169.254.169.254#@public.example', 80); same for 'http://127.0.0.1%23@public.example/x' and 'http://a%2f@public.example/x'; plain 'http://public.example/x' connects to the vetted 93.184.216.34. https URLs stay pinned. unshare -n strace of getaddrinfo('169.254.169.254#@public.example'): no DNS socket opened, EAI_NONAME (a valid name opens UDP sockets to the nameservers).
issues.suggested_fix: Use urllib's own state: proxied = req.has_proxy() (selector == full_url after set_proxy), or record the proxy decision in a ProxyHandler subclass; and reject URLs with userinfo or '%' in the netloc in unsafe_url_reason (urllib cannot fetch them correctly anyway).

issues.problem: The new short-sentence rule counts any digit, including citation markers, table/figure numbers and list numbers, so honest navigational sentences in a findings section ('Results are in Table 2.', 'See Figure 3 below.', 'We compared 4 vendors.') become uncited factual claims and fail --strict; a report that passed at 197a8d6 now fails. Short digit-free factual claims still escape the gate entirely ('Acme is HIPAA compliant.', 'Acme never had a breach.', 'Microsoft owns Acme outright.' are never extracted). The docstring says short factual sentences must not slip past the gate; the limit is not documented.
